Resolves #19006

The month view's grid now has its structure witness. `MonthGridStructure.spec.mjs` mounts the `calendar-month` fixture at a fixed February 2027 and asserts the window as literal id lists: 18 weeks of 7 cells, row index 6 as the week holding the 1st with its month header directly before it, the August wrap, weekend cells following the day rather than the column, the runtime `weekStartDay` change rebuilding rows and day-name header, and `showWeekends: false` leaving 90 of the 126 cells. Every expected date was derived by hand from `getFirstDayOffset` and written out in the file; the spec never reads its expectations back off the helper or the component.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, the component tier locally and in CI) → L3 required (the component-tier witness ACs). No residuals.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | the fixture `test/playwright/component/apps/calendar-month/`: `currentDate` fixed at 2027-02-01, `weekStartDay` movable at runtime through the state provider, asserted after the move in arms 4 and 6 |
| AC-2 | `test/playwright/component/calendar/MonthGridStructure.spec.mjs`, seven arms; every 18-row window appears as a literal (`FEB_ROWS`, `FEB_ROWS_WSD1`, `AUG_ROWS_WSD0`, `AUG_ROWS_WSD1`) plus the row-6 cell lists |
| AC-3 | fixture fixes `currentDate`; locale pinned in `neo-config.json` (receipt below); every arm opens the fixture itself, and a single arm passes standalone |
| AC-4 | arm 4: rows rebuild for `weekStartDay: 1`, weekend to the last two cells; arm 6: day-name header Sun..Sat then Mon..Sun |
| AC-5 | `npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/calendar/`: 11 passed locally on `8ce4205b1a`; CI runs the same tier across its `components` shards |
| AC-6 | the diff is `test/` only; no file under `src/` is changed |

## Deltas from ticket
- The no-calendars case in the ticket's list is already witnessed by `MonthEmptyMount.spec.mjs` (merged with #19150), the 126 cells on an empty mount included. This spec takes the structural cases; the empty-mount case stays in that file.
- The fixture's locale pin lives in `neo-config.json`, not in `modelData`. Through `modelData` alone the value differs from the default during the application construct and fires `DateSelector.afterSetLocale`, which throws before the page mounts. In the config it seeds the state provider as well, so the mount writes nothing.
- `driver.mjs` gains `setCurrentDate`, `setWeekStartDay` and `setShowWeekends`, each writing through the state provider, the same path the app's own date selector and settings take.
- Arm 4's write order (`weekStartDay` before the month) is a workaround for #19172, found here: run the other way round, the sidebar `DateSelector` reads a vdom the second write has reshaped and the fixtures' error gate fails the test.

## Test Evidence
- `npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/calendar/` on `8ce4205b1a`, after rebasing over current `dev`: 11 passed (7 here, 4 `MonthEmptyMount`).
- Mutation, the wrap's teeth: with only `getFirstDayOffset`'s negative wrap removed (`return firstDayOffset` in place of `firstDayOffset < 0 ? firstDayOffset + 7 : firstDayOffset`), arm 4 reads its August window one week late: first row `2027-06-21`, last row `2027-10-18`, where `2027-06-14` and `2027-10-11` are expected. The other six arms pass. Restored byte-identical; `src/` is clean.
- Locale pin, its teeth: configured as `de-DE`, exactly the two arms that read day names fail (arm 6's header, arm 4's sidebar step); both pass again with `en-US` restored.
- `agent-preflight`: not hosted here (no `ai/` tree). The pinned `pr-body` checker (`neo-agent-skills@0.1.16`) and the commit-time `lint-staged` guards ran locally instead.

# PR Micro-Review

**Opening:** Thank you, @sloemo01, especially for two choices. You derived the four windows by hand and gave the wrap its teeth with a mutation, instead of reading the expectations back off `getFirstDayOffset`. And you found out why the locale pin has to live in `neo-config.json`. Both are the judgement the ticket was really asking for. Your one entry point from here is #19172. It's the crash your weekend arm steps around, filed from your finding and reserved for you. The red arm is half-written already: it's arm 4 run in the other order.

**Class:** mechanical. The PR is test-only: one spec plus fixture driver actions and a locale pin. It changes no `src/` file and teaches no architectural concept.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:**
- **Premise:** an 18-week window with the 1st in row 6, the August wrap, `neo-weekend` following the day, a runtime `weekStartDay` rebuild, and 90 cells with weekends off.
- **Checked against my own derivation from `createContent()` and `getFirstDayOffset`:** all four literal windows match. February runs `2026-12-20`→`2027-04-18` (and `-12-21`→`-04-19` at `weekStartDay: 1`). August runs `06-20`→`10-17` (and `06-14`→`10-11`).
- **At exact head `f42ce1f9b3`:** CI is green, component shards included, and locally 11 tests pass.
- **An extra mutation you didn't list:** making `neo-weekend` follow the column instead of the day turns exactly arm 4 red, with the other 6 green. So arm 4 alone carries the day-not-column claim; arm 5's Sunday-start row can't tell the two apart. That's fine as written.
- **The one thing I looked for and found:** arm 4's comment describes a `src/` crash that the PR body doesn't mention. I reproduced it: moving the month and then `weekStartDay` back to back throws `Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'transform')` from `DateSelector`, and the fixtures' error gate fails the test. #19006 asks for a red against `src/` to be reported, so it is now #19172.

**Findings:**

- [ ] Cite #19172 in arm 4's ordering comment, since it's the crash that comment describes. Add one line to the PR body's Deltas saying the write order is a workaround for #19172, found here. Nothing else changes.
